strategy: Start with cartservice pod recovery, then test the high-reach product-catalog slowdown; both can affect shoppers across the site. Follow with the distinct checkout-error and frontend-load scenarios, using different services and four different failure classes overall.

spec.reason: Ranked first because cartservice is a single replica, has high risk, and reaches all five flows as well as the checkout path. Prior cartservice pod-kill runs produced errors across all flows and roughly 22–24 seconds to pod readiness, making this a direct shopper-visible recovery test.
spec.hypothesis: Shoppers will see errors and severe latency across the flows while cartservice is unavailable; Kubernetes will replace the pod and the experiment will complete.

experiments.learning_goal: Measure the customer impact and recovery time when the single cartservice replica is killed.

spec.reason: productcatalogservice is a single replica, has reach 1.0, and is on every flow and the checkout path. Past 100 ms delays affected all flows and raised p95 to about 716–757 ms; this 300 ms recipe is large enough to be shopper-visible, though the guard may abort if the slowdown exceeds its limit.
spec.hypothesis: All flows that call the catalog will become severely slower without necessarily returning errors; the high added latency may trip the p95 guard and abort injection.

experiments.learning_goal: See how a stronger catalog latency fault propagates across user journeys and whether the safety guard limits exposure.

spec.reason: paymentservice is a single-replica dependency on the checkout revenue path. Past 30-second outages affected checkout, with peak error rate around 21% and runs sometimes aborted by the error guard; shoppers attempting checkout should see the failure.
spec.hypothesis: Checkout requests will error while other flows remain largely unaffected; the error rate is likely to exceed the guard threshold and abort the experiment.

experiments.learning_goal: Measure the checkout blast radius and guard response when payment processing is unavailable.

spec.reason: frontend is the single-replica entrypoint for every shopper request. Prior 100- and 150-user spikes slowed all flows, with peak p95 around 1.0–1.16 seconds; 200 users tests a more visible load while staying below the prior 300-user guard-triggering level.
spec.hypothesis: The frontend and its dependencies will slow across all flows under 200 concurrent shoppers, but are likely to remain below the 1500 ms p95 guard with no errors.

experiments.learning_goal: Determine how much additional shopper-visible latency appears between the previously tested 150-user load and the guard-sensitive 300-user load.

skipped_ideas.why_not: Prior runs made failures visible across all flows but triggered the error guard and caused cartservice recovery; traffic_spike covers resource exhaustion here while using a different service from the cartservice recovery test.
A prior run already showed severe shopper-visible slowdown and was stopped by the p95 guard; the plan uses the checkout outage for the distinct error-class test instead.
